measured_development_probe.surface: released dependency-free zipapp through the real loopback HTTP API and SQLite state

weakness.name: unbounded and nonpositive approval lifetime
weakness.observed: The released API accepts a negative TTL, creates and audits an already-expired approval, transitions the proposal from pending to approved, rejects execution as expired, and then rejects a valid recovery approval because the proposal is no longer pending.
weakness.coverage_gap: The frozen evaluation grades default-TTL approval, execution, sequential idempotency, replay, postconditions, and exact terminal state but contains zero invalid-lifetime or lifetime-boundary cases.
weakness.security_implication: Code inspection shows the same unchecked integer input also permits approval lifetimes longer than the declared short-lived default. This is an inference from the released validation path and is not presented as a separate observed exploit.
weakness.highest_leverage_reason: A small deterministic policy boundary can prevent both a measured benign liveness failure and unbounded approval lifetime without changing the agent, retrieval, action surface, executor, credentials, or real-infrastructure boundary.

selected_boundary.invalid_request_result: HTTP 400 before proposal, approval, audit, incident, or trace mutation
selected_boundary.source: project-authored policy using the existing 300-second default; no external source or asset

retained_tooling_failures: The first probe combined Start-Process with a large inline PowerShell body and was rejected by local command policy before launch or state creation. The same released-package experiment then ran through the repository's in-process loopback-server pattern.
next_gate: freeze the approval-lifetime contract and milestone before implementation
